study_id: Wang et al. - 2022 - Comparison of Four Machine Learning Techniques for Prediction of Intensive Care Unit Length of Stay

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: Although the study involves adult heart transplant recipients and uses non‑linear machine learning models, its primary outcome is ICU length of stay, which is not among the specified eligible outcomes (survival, waitlist mortality, post‑transplant complications, quality of life, or economic measures).

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective study of 365 heart transplantation patients to predict ICU length of stay using machine learning.
identification_methods.Institution: Department of Cardiovascular Surgery, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Clinical data from Wuhan Union Hospital electronic medical records
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included consecutive adult heart transplantation patients (365) from April 2017 to August 2020.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: XGBoost, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression
identification_methods.Input Variables: 84 clinical features initially; six key variables selected (ECMO, donor age, IABP, surgery length, creatinine, CRRT)
identification_methods.Methods Notes: LASSO regression for feature selection, SHAP values for model interpretation, online web‑server for prediction.

population.Inclusion criteria: Heart transplantation surgery for moderate (NYHA grade 3) or severe (NYHA grade 4) heart failure
population.Population Notes: Patients randomly divided into training (N=256) and test (N=109) sets; 84 clinical features collected

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: XGBoost, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: 84 clinical features collected; 6 selected by LASSO for final model
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Five‑fold cross‑validation, up‑sampling for class imbalance, SHAP values for model interpretation, online web‑server tool
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Prediction of intensive care unit length of stay (ICU‑LOS) with metrics AUC‑ROC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is binary classification of prolonged vs short ICU stay
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: XGBoost achieved the highest performance (AUC‑ROC = 0.8828) compared with other models
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported name: ICU length of stay (prolonged vs short)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: Logistic regression and other machine‑learning models (RF, NB, SVM)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC‑ROC calculated on a completely held‑out test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: XGBoost significantly outperformed logistic regression and other ML models for ICU‑LOS prediction
